title: Architecture & Standards: Unified API, Coding, Infra, Model-Serving, Observability, and Performance Guidelines (ADRs)
author: Aisha Kapoor
content:
Overview

Purpose: This document consolidates Redwood Inference's architecture and engineering standards for API design, coding practices, infrastructure, model-serving, observability, and performance. It includes prescriptive rules, ownership, SLOs/thresholds, and a small set of Decision Records (ADRs) for recent cross-cutting decisions. Use this as the canonical reference for new services and changes to existing systems.

Audience: Engineers, architects, technical program managers, and SREs.

1) High-level principles
- API-first and backward-compatible: prioritize clear, versioned contracts; maintain at least one stable minor version for 12 months unless security-critical changes are required.
- Production-first: every service must define SLOs, error budgets, and automated health checks before rollout.
- Observable by design: instrument traces, metrics, and structured logs for business and system-level insights.
- Secure defaults: apply least-privilege networking, encryption-in-transit and at-rest, and authenticated service-to-service calls.

2) API standards (owner: API Platform)
- Surface: REST + JSON by default; gRPC allowed for high-throughput internal RPCs. Public endpoints must provide OpenAPI v3 spec and example SDK snippets.
- Versioning: semantic versioning for public APIs: /v{major}/...; breaking changes increment major or create a new route. Minor/patch changes must be backward-compatible.
- Contract: every request/response must include a stable schema and field-level descriptions. Use snake_case for JSON keys for consistency with existing SDKs.
- Error handling: use HTTP status codes with a structured error body {"code": string, "message": string, "details": optional list}. Standard codes: 400, 401, 403, 404, 409 (conflict), 429 (rate limit), 500. Include a machine-readable error.code (e.g. model_not_loaded, quota_exceeded).
- Rate limiting: token-bucket per-API-key + global service-level limits. Default burst: 200 r/s per key for hosted endpoints; Dedicated/Private customers have contract-specific limits.
- API Review checklist (pre-merge): OpenAPI spec included, automated contract tests (schema + example), changelog entry, and migration plan for breaking changes.

3) Coding standards (owner: Eng DX)
- Languages and style: follow repository-specific style guides. Default linters: eslint (JS/TS), gofmt + golangci-lint (Go), black/flake8 (Python).
- Modular services: small, focused services with clear public interfaces. Prefer composition over monoliths.
- Tests: unit tests >= 80% coverage for business logic; integration tests for downstream dependencies; contract tests for APIs. All tests must run in CI.
- Dependency policy: pin transitive dependencies for minor security-sensitive services. Security team approves exceptions.
- Secrets: never commit secrets. Use Vault (or cloud KMS) and environment injection in CI/CD.
- CI: every PR must run lint, unit tests, integration smoke tests, and do a small security scan (Snyk/Trivy). Merge only after 2 approvers for service-critical repos.

4) Infrastructure standards (owner: Eng Infra)
- IaC: Terraform 1.x modules for cloud accounts, VPCs, and common infra. Module registry and versioning required.
- Network: default deny across namespaces; east-west traffic uses mTLS. Public ingress through API Gateway with WAF rules and rate limiting.
- IAM: least privilege with role separation; use short-lived credentials for service accounts.
- Capacity & autoscaling: define target utilization (see SRE section). Autoscaling policies require cooldowns and safe-guards to prevent oscillation.
- Cost tagging: all cloud resources must include tags: owner, cost-center, environment, service. Missing tags block deploy via pre-deploy CI hook.

5) Model-serving standards (owner: Serving Runtime)
- Model catalog: every served model must have manifest metadata: model_id, semantic_version, input_shape, max_context, quantization_profiles, supported_kernels, and a short performance profile (p50/p95 latency for typical request sizes).
- Deployment patterns: blue/green or canary rollouts mandatory for model updates in production. Canary size: default 1-5% of traffic with automatic rollback on error rate or quality regression.
- Compatibility: runtime must expose compatible model variants and fallback policies. E.g., if a quantized variant is unavailable, runtime can fallback to full-precision with rate-limited traffic.
- KV caching: standard prefix caching and shared KV store for repeated prefixes (configurable TTL). Cache hit-rate and staleness instruments required.
- Quantization and kernels: quantization profiles must be validated in the QA cluster; kernel selection must be logged with metrics for traceability.
- Model quality checks: each model release must include a regression test suite (eval by prompt sets) and pass quality gates (no more than X% drop vs baseline on critical metrics).

6) Observability standards (owner: Eng Platform + SRE)
- Telemetry: required signals: metrics (Prometheus), traces (OpenTelemetry), structured logs (JSON).
- Naming conventions: metrics use kebab-case with service prefix: service_name.metric_name{labels}. Histogram buckets defined in performance section.
- Tracing: propagate trace_id and span_id for every external request. Client sampling 0.5% by default; increase for canary/debug.
- Dashboards & alerts: every service must ship at least: 1) health dashboard, 2) latency distribution, 3) error rate, 4) resource utilization. Alerts should map to runbooks.
- Log retention: default 30 days for development, 90 days for production; extended retention via request to data-compliance. Logs must avoid PII.

7) Performance standards & SLOs (owner: Eng SRE)
- Baseline SLOs for public inference (hosted API): uptime >= 99.95% per region (monthly), p95 latency <= 350ms for short-form generation (<= 128 tokens) on curated model variants. p99 targets are set per-model in the catalog.
- Error budget policy: monthly error budget = 100% - SLO. Use standard burn-rate alerts: 14-day and 3-day burn rate thresholds trigger actions (review, canary pause, throttling).
- Resource targets: GPU utilization target 60-75% during steady-state; burst headroom reserved for 10% of capacity.
- Batching policy: automatic batching must be enabled for high-throughput routes; max batch size chosen to meet latency SLO for target percentile.

8) Runbooks and incident process (owner: Eng SRE)
- On-call rotations: 2-week primary rotation and 4-week secondary rotation. Pager duty rules map to service SLO severity.
- Incident steps (high-level): 1) Triage + acknowledge, 2) Ramp to page teams, 3) Hotfix/mitigation, 4) Postmortem within 72 hours, 5) Follow-up fixes and ADR if needed.
- Postmortem template: summary, timeline, impact, root cause, corrective actions, owners, and MTTD/MTTR metrics.

9) Decision Records (ADRs) included
- ADR 2025-11: Default API surface = REST + JSON
  - Decision: Use REST+JSON for public API and gRPC for internal high-throughput paths.
  - Rationale: SDK friendliness, web compatibility, and ecosystem maturity.
  - Consequences: Require OpenAPI specs and contract tests for public APIs.

- ADR 2025-12: Quantization as first-class deployment option
  - Decision: Allow quantized model variants in production with validated profiles.
  - Rationale: Cost-per-token savings materially improves economics.
  - Consequences: Add model manifest fields and mandatory QA regression suites.

- ADR 2026-01: Observability standardization on OpenTelemetry + Prometheus
  - Decision: Adopt OpenTelemetry for tracing and Prometheus for core metrics.
  - Rationale: Standardized tooling across teams simplifies correlation and onboarding.
  - Consequences: Instrumentation libraries and templated dashboards required for new services.

10) Templates and checklists (attachments)
- API review checklist: OpenAPI, contract tests, migration plan, changelog.
- Service onboarding checklist: SLOs defined, dashboards created, runbooks added, cost tags present.
- Model deployment checklist: manifest, QA evals, canary plan, rollback plan.

11) Example configurations
- Prometheus scrape targets (example table):
| service | scrape_interval | retention |
| redwood-inference-api | 15s | 90d |
| model-serving-runtime | 10s | 90d |

- Sample error response JSON (public API):
{
  "status": 429,
  "error": {
    "code": "rate_limited",
    "message": "Rate limit exceeded for API key",
    "retry_after_seconds": 30
  }
}

12) Ownership and governance
- Owners: API Platform (API standards), Eng DX (coding), Eng Infra (infra), Serving Runtime (model serving), Eng Platform + SRE (observability), Eng SRE (performance).
- Standards review cadence: quarterly reviews and ADRs for major changes. Emergency ADRs allowed for security incidents.
- How to propose changes: open a PR against this page repo, add ADR if the change is architectural, run a 2-week review with stakeholders listed in the reviewers section.

Appendix A: Helpful links
- Runtime architecture: /confluence/eng-serving-runtime/runtime-architecture
- SLO and error budgets: /confluence/eng-sre/slo-and-error-budgets
- IaC module registry: /confluence/eng-infra/terraform-and-iac

Appendix B: Glossary
- P50/P95/P99: latency percentiles.
- ADR: Architecture Decision Record.
- KV cache: prefix-based key-value caching used to reduce token compute for repeated prompts.

Contact: For questions about interpretation or edge cases, contact the owners listed above or open an issue in the standards repo.
